data.title: Consumer Review Platforms Used to Carry the Narrative
data.summary:
Review and rating platforms were used to carry campaign claims, with clusters of
accounts posting coordinated negative reviews referencing the campaign narrative rather
than any transaction.
data.description:
Review platforms are attractive because their output is durable, highly ranked in search,
and read by people making decisions. A review persists long after a social media post has
scrolled away, and it reaches customers at the moment of choice.

Coordination is usually visible in the detail: reviews that describe no specific
transaction, cluster tightly in time, reuse phrasing, and arrive from accounts with no
other review history. Several platforms expose reviewer history, which makes this one of
the more evidentially solid parts of such an analysis.

Each platform has a manipulation policy and a specific evidence format. The quality of
the report submitted matters more than the fact of reporting, and a well-evidenced
submission is frequently actioned where a complaint is not.
data.recommendation:
* Collect reviewer history, timing and phrasing overlap into the evidence package each
  platform's manipulation policy requires.
* Report through the platform's manipulation route rather than disputing reviews
  individually.
* Do not solicit offsetting positive reviews; it breaches the same policies and
  undermines any later complaint.
data.short_recommendation: Report under platform manipulation policy with a full evidence package.
